title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons, describe the natural world, and say what is about to happen ('it's going to rain').
intro: Tamil Nadu is hot most of the year — Chennai jokes that it has three seasons: hot, hotter and hottest — and gets most of its rain from the **north-east monsoon** in October–December. Tamil weather expressions use specific verbs: rain **falls** (பெய்), the sun **beats** (அடி), wind **blows** (அடி / வீசு).

vocab.note: மழை பெய்யுது 'it's raining'; past பெஞ்சுது penjudu

phrases.en: It's very hot and sunny today.
It looks like it's going to rain.
It gets very cold in Ooty.
Apparently a cyclone is coming tomorrow.
There's been little rain this year.

grammar.title: Weather expressions
grammar.body:
Weather uses specific noun + verb pairs, usually in the neuter (-உது / -உம்) form:

**மழை பெய்யுது** — rain is falling (it's raining)
**வெயில் அடிக்குது** — the sun is beating (it's hot and sunny)
**காத்து அடிக்குது / வீசுது** — wind is blowing
**குளிருது** — it's cold (lit. it chills)
**இடி இடிக்குது** — it's thundering
**வேர்க்குது** — (I'm) sweating

For a state, use **-ஆ இருக்கு**: சூடா இருக்கு 'it's hot', குளிரா இருக்கு 'it's cold', மேகமா இருக்கு 'it's cloudy'. The neuter future **-உம்** expresses general truths: சென்னையில மே மாசம் ரொம்ப வெயில் அடிக்கும் 'In Chennai it's very hot in May'.

examples.en: It's cold in the month of Margazhi.
There's always a good breeze on the beach.

grammar.title: 'It's going to…': -ப் போகுது, மாதிரி இருக்கு, and -ஆம் (hearsay)
grammar.body:
To say something **is about to happen**, use the infinitive + **போ** 'go' in the present: **மழை பெய்யப் போகுது** 'it's going to rain', **நான் சாப்பிடப் போறேன்** 'I'm going to eat'. This is the Tamil 'going to'.

To say something **looks like** it will happen, use the relative participle + **மாதிரி இருக்கு** 'it's like': மழை வர்ற மாதிரி இருக்கு 'it looks like rain'.

A handy spoken suffix: **-ஆம்** *-ām* on a verb means 'reportedly / they say': புயல் வருமாம் 'apparently a cyclone will come', மழை பெய்யுமாம் 'they say it'll rain'.

examples.en: It's gone dark — it's going to rain.
The bus is about to leave, come quickly!
It looks like it'll be sunny today.

dialogue.title: A cyclone warning
dialogue.setting: Meena and her neighbour Sarah chat on the terrace in November.

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.native: ஆமா, நாளைக்குப் புயல் வருமாம். டிவில சொன்னாங்க.
lines.roman: āmā, nāḷaikkup puyal varumām. ṭīvila sonnānga.
lines.en: Yes, apparently a cyclone is coming tomorrow. They said so on TV.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Oh no! Is it a very big cyclone?

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.en: I don't know. But they say there'll be a lot of rain.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Does it always rain like this in Chennai?

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.native: இல்ல, மழைக்காலத்துல மட்டும். மத்த மாசம் எல்லாம் வெயில்தான்!
lines.roman: illa, maḻaikkālattula maṭṭum. matta māsam ellām veyildān!
lines.en: No, only in the rainy season. All the other months it's just sun!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Will the office be open tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.native: லீவு விடுவாங்கன்னு நினைக்கிறேன். தண்ணி, மெழுகுவர்த்தி எல்லாம் வாங்கி வைங்க.
lines.roman: līvu viḍuvāngannu ninaikkirēn. taṇṇi, meḻuguvartti ellām vāngi vainga.
lines.en: I think they'll declare a holiday. Buy and keep water, candles and so on.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: சரி. இப்போவே மழை பெய்யப் போகுது, உள்ள போலாம்!
lines.roman: sari. ippōvē maḻai peyyap pōgudu, uḷḷa pōlām!
lines.en: OK. It's about to rain right now — let's go inside!

culture: Classical Tamil poetry divides the land into five landscapes (திணை *tiṇai*) — mountains, forest, farmland, seashore and desert — each linked to a mood of love. Today, people in hot Tamil Nadu welcome rain joyfully, and the cool month of **Margazhi** (mid-December–mid-January) is Chennai's famous music and dance season.

tip.title: Sun beats, wind blows
tip.body:
- Weather is a noun plus its own verb, in the 'it' form **-உது**: **வெயில் அடிக்குது** 'the sun is beating down', **காத்து அடிக்குது / வீசுது** 'the wind is blowing'.
- For a state use **-ஆ இருக்கு**: வெயில்**ஆ** இருக்கு, சூடா இருக்கு, மேகமா இருக்கு.
- Sweating has no 'I': **வேர்க்குது** 'it sweats (me)'.

sentences.en: It's sunny today.

sentences.native: வெளிய ரொம்ப வெயிலா இருக்கு, உள்ள வாங்க.
sentences.roman: veḷiya romba veyilā irukku, uḷḷa vānga.
sentences.en: It's really hot out there, come inside.
It was very hot and sunny yesterday.
Madurai gets very hot in summer.
There's a good breeze this evening.
Switch the fan on, I'm sweating.
You can't even see the sun today, it's cloudy.
What's the weather like?
There's no breeze at all today.
Don't go out in the midday sun.

tip.title: Rain falls: மழை பெய்யுது
tip.body:
- Rain has its own verb **பெய்**: **மழை பெய்யுது** 'it's raining', past **மழை பெஞ்சுது** 'it rained'.
- Thunder thunders: **இடி இடிக்குது**.
- States again use **-ஆ இருக்கு**: ஈரமா இருக்கு 'it's wet', தெளிவா இருக்கு 'it's clear'.
- Ask with **-ஆ**: மழை பெய்யு**தா**? 'is it raining?'

sentences.en: Is it raining outside?
It rained a lot last night.
It's thundering, don't go outside.
It's raining, with thunder and lightning.
The sky has gone dark.
The floor is wet, watch your step.
The clothes are still wet.

sentences.native: இப்போ மழை இல்ல, வானம் தெளிவா இருக்கு.
sentences.roman: ippō maḻai illa, vānam teḷivā irukku.
sentences.en: There's no rain now, the sky is clear.

tip.title: What it is usually like: -உம்
tip.body:
- **-உது** is what's happening now: **குளிருது** 'it's cold (now)'.
- **-உம்** is what generally happens: **குளிரும்** 'it gets cold', **மழை பெய்யும்** 'it rains (then)'.
- Negative of -உம் is **-ஆது**: **குளிராது** 'it doesn't get cold'.
- Seasons take -ல: மழைக்காலத்**துல** 'in the rainy season'.

sentences.en: It rains a lot in the rainy season.
Mornings are cold in winter.
It's really cold now, please shut the window.
It doesn't get that cold in Chennai.
Cyclones come in the rainy season.
There was a big flood last year.
When there's a cyclone, school is closed.
It's colder than usual this year.
Shall we walk by the sea this evening?
The moon is beautiful tonight.
There are lots of stars in the sky.

sentences.native: எங்க ஊர் பக்கத்துல ஒரு நதி இருக்கு.
sentences.roman: enga ūr pakkattula oru nadi irukku.
sentences.en: There's a river near our town.

sentences.native: வீட்டு முன்னாடி ஒரு பெரிய மரம் இருக்கு.
sentences.roman: vīṭṭu munnāḍi oru periya maram irukku.
sentences.en: There's a big tree in front of the house.
There are lots of plants on the terrace.
I love yellow flowers.
I love nature.
It gets cold at night in the hills.

tip.title: Going to, looks like, apparently
tip.body:
- **Going to**: infinitive + **போகுது / போறேன்**: மழை பெய்ய**ப் போகுது**, நான் குளிக்க**ப் போறேன்**.
- **Looks like**: the '-ing' form (வர்ற, பெய்யுற, தூங்குற) + **மாதிரி இருக்கு**: மழை வர்ற **மாதிரி இருக்கு**.
- **Apparently, they say**: add **-ஆம்** to the verb: புயல் வரு**மாம்**, குளிரு**தாம்**.
tip.pattern: verb-அ + போகுது  ·  verb-ற + மாதிரி இருக்கு  ·  verb + ஆம்

sentences.en: It's getting dark, it's going to rain.
I'm going to have a bath.
The train's about to come, hurry up.

sentences.native: குடை எடுத்துக்கோங்க, மழை பெய்யுற மாதிரி இருக்கு.
sentences.roman: kuḍai eḍuttukkōnga, maḻai peyyura mādiri irukku.
sentences.en: Take an umbrella, it looks like rain.
Looks like the baby is asleep.
Apparently it'll be very hot tomorrow.
Apparently it's really cold in Ooty right now.
Did you bring an umbrella?
